chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of was from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā; and from Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Musallī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the ghusl of the deceased. He said: "A cloth is placed over him, then his private part is washed, and he is given wudu (ablution) like the wudu of salat (prayer). Then his head is washed with lote leaves and ushnān, then with water and camphor, then with pure water, in which seven sound leaves are placed in the water."

key_terms.السِّدْرِ: lote leaves used in washing the deceased
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor mixed with water in one stage of the washing
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْقَرَاحِ: pure unmixed water used in the final washing
key_terms.خِرْقَةٌ: a cloth placed over the deceased during preparation
key_terms.سَبْعُ وَرَقَاتٍ صِحَاحٍ: seven intact leaves placed in the water
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased person
key_terms.فَرْجُهُ: his private part, washed as part of the funeral ghusl
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: the wudu (ablution) performed like that of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: How is the ghusl of the deceased performed according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the procedure for the ghusl of the deceased, beginning with covering the body, washing the private part, and performing wudu (ablution). It then outlines successive washings with sidr and ushnan, with water and camphor, and finally with pure water containing seven intact leaves.
